timeline.from_level: 20 bodyweight squats, 8 split squats per side, pain-free deep knee flexion
timeline.human_label: 4–8 months from a solid split squat
timeline.notes: No named coach publishes a shrimp-squat timeline. These numbers are interpolated from the pistol tree, which OG2 places at a comparable level, adjusted upward slightly for the greater knee-flexion and quad-length demand. Treat as an order-of-magnitude guide.

prerequisite_standards.name: Split squats
prerequisite_standards.rationale: Baseline unilateral strength in a split stance.

prerequisite_standards.name: Pain-free deep knee flexion
prerequisite_standards.target: heel to glute, kneeling, no pain
prerequisite_standards.rationale: The rear leg is fully flexed throughout — this is the actual gate.

prerequisite_standards.name: Quad flexibility
prerequisite_standards.rationale: A short rectus femoris pulls the pelvis into tilt and makes the shape impossible.

plateau_signatures.signal: Rear hamstring cramps before the working leg is challenged
typical_causes: Rear leg held actively rather than relaxed
Insufficient quad and hip-flexor length on the rear side
resolution: Hold the rear foot rather than actively pulling it
Add quad and hip-flexor length work before sessions

plateau_signatures.signal: Strong enough on box shrimps but topples at the bottom of the full range
resolution: Hold a light counterweight at arms' length
Practise fresh at the start of the session

injury_risk_timeline.mechanism: Deep flexion on the working leg combined with the rear knee contacting the floor
prophylaxis: Progress via box height over 8–12 weeks rather than by forcing depth
Stop the set when the descent stops being controlled
red_flags: Patellar tendon pain at the bottom
